First row per problem_index, then n_generated >= 12000, cap hits included. Header test: re.match of the given regex on each line of text.split('
'); line offset = cumulative len(line)+1; counted iff some header line starts at >= L/2 (float L/2) and none at < L/2. Statistic = counted / kept, bootstrap over kept problems. The text field includes the 3 prefilled cue tokens (' line!

Okay'), so L counts them; this shifts the midpoint by about 6 characters. Alt reading (alt_measured): line boundaries from str.splitlines() (also splits on , \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, \x85,  ,  ), which can change offsets and which lines match. Not done: measuring halves in tokens (no tokenizer allowed). refuted_by is null so refuted_by_met is always false; zero kept rows would print not_computable. example_row has text and prompt truncated (text_len added).

Same file as k=2. First row per problem_index; rows with missing or null score_v3 dropped; keep cap_hit is False, score_v3 == 1, n_generated > 10000 (strictly greater, and 10000, not the 12000 of prediction 1: the recipe says so explicitly). r uses prediction 1's definition from drafts/r6-m01.json (its recipe only was read): decile k = t[floor((k-1)L/10):floor(kL/10)] with integer floor, re.findall of (?<![A-Za-z])(Let me|I'm|I'll|Okay|Wait|Hmm|I|me)(?![A-Za-z]) case-sensitive within each decile slice; M_early = d2+d3, M_late = d8+d9; r = (M_late+1)/(M_early+1). Statistic = statistics.median (mean of two middle values for even count), bootstrap over kept problems. Lookbehind/lookahead are evaluated inside the slice, so a slice edge acts as a non-letter boundary (a word cut at a decile edge such as 'I' from 'If' can be counted). Alt reading (alt_measured): finditer over the whole text, each match assigned to the decile containing its start offset. Text includes the prefilled cue ('Okay' in decile 1 only, so it does not enter r). Zero kept rows prints refuted_without_number as the recipe says. Base-only statistic; no RL subtraction (the experiment compares to about 1.0 directly). Small n is likely (long answers that finish right are rare), so the interval may be wide.
